test_title: PYST 2: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A sofa is marked at ₹5,000 and sold for ₹4,250 after two successive discounts of 10% and a certain percentage. What is the second discount?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

After 10% discount ⇒ Price = 5000 × 0.9 = 4500

Final SP = 4250

⇒ Reduction = 4500 − 4250 = 250

⇒ Second discount = (250 ÷ 4500) × 100 ≈ 5.56%

**∴ Answer = 5.56%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price = 5000

First discount = 10%

Selling Price = 4250

**Formula:**

SP = MP × (1 − d₁) × (1 − d₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4250 = 5000 × 0.9 × (1 − d₂)

⇒ 4250 = 4500 × (1 − d₂)

⇒ (1 − d₂) = 4250 ÷ 4500 = 0.9444

⇒ d₂ = 1 − 0.9444 = 0.0556

⇒ d₂ = 5.56%

**∴ Second Discount = 5.56%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Successive Discount Formula:** Net Discount = a + b − (ab ÷ 100)

**Multiplier Method:** Final Price = MP × (1 − d₁) × (1 − d₂)

**Approximation Trick:** Small discounts can be quickly estimated using ratio reduction.

**Important Insight:** Second discount always applies on reduced price, not on MP.
